stage_a.note: Founder smiles frequently and maintains an upbeat, enthusiastic tone throughout the pitch.
He shows sustained excitement while demonstrating the hats and placing them on the bananas.
He uses friendly, relatable language to connect with the panel about a common household problem.

venture.description: Silicone caps with magnetic knitted hats designed to slow the ripening process of bananas by blocking ethylene gas.
venture.note: The product is designed to reduce food waste and add a decorative element to the kitchen.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder pitches a silicone cap and knitted hat device that slows banana ripening by blocking ethylene gas, asking for $150k.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori asks if the device works by covering the top of the bananas to prevent the release of ethylene gas.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms that the gas is still emitted but the device slows its spread to the other bananas.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks how many days the device extends the freshness of the bananas.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states they do not make specific claims but estimates it extends freshness by eight to twelve days.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter acknowledges that extending the freshness by that amount of time is a solid value proposition.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond asks if the green plastic wrap found on store-bought bananas serves the same preservation purpose.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms that the plastic wrap uses the exact same methodology to preserve the fruit.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond remarks that he learns something new every day, showing appreciation for the explanation.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks for the retail selling price and the cost to manufacture the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states they sell a two-pack for twelve ninety-nine and the landed cost is one ninety-five.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin points out that producing just the silicone sock without the magnet would be significantly cheaper.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder briefly confirms Kevin's statement that removing the magnet would lower the manufacturing cost.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin challenges the design complexity, asking why he could not just put a smiley face directly on the silicone sock.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder defends the design, arguing that a plain sock is visually unappealing on a kitchen counter.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin laughs at the founder's humorous defense of the product's aesthetics.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark joins in the laughter regarding the founder's comment about the unappealing silicone sock.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks the founder what inspired him to invent this particular product.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter chimes in to ask why he specifically named the product Nana Hats.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains he was trying to keep his bananas fresh and found that existing methods were inconsistent and wasteful.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter asks what the founder does for a living outside of this business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder reveals he currently works as a wealth manager for a large investment bank.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond laughs loudly at the contrast between the founder's serious day job and his novelty product.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter shares a laugh over the unexpected revelation about the founder's professional background.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark is highly amused and laughs at the founder's career in finance.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin also laughs, finding the situation deeply entertaining.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder continues his story, explaining that working from home gave him the time to launch the company.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter asks what has happened with the business since the initial launch.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder reveals that for the full year of 2021, the business generated four hundred eighty-three thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin expresses surprise and approval at the impressive revenue figure.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter is visibly shocked and impressed by the high sales numbers achieved.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark enthusiastically cheers for the success of the banana preservation business.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter follows up by asking what the projected sales are for the current year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states they are projecting six hundred thousand in sales and two hundred forty thousand in profit.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori expresses amazement at the strong projected sales and profit margins.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter asks for the breakdown of sales between retail channels and direct-to-consumer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder clarifies that sixty percent of sales are direct-to-consumer and forty percent are wholesale.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks where exactly the product is being placed in retail environments.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains that almost all wholesale sales go through one large online gift retailer, with some novelty shops.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks if the founder has attempted to pitch the product to grocery chains.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori echoes Kevin's question, asking specifically if he has reached out to large grocery chains like Kroger.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder says he has been making calls and emails but acknowledges that it is a brand new product category.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark thinks the idea is insane and declines to invest, though he congratulates the founder on the impressive sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder thanks Mark for his kind words despite him dropping out of the deal.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark reiterates his congratulations to the founder for successfully selling a quirky product.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond asserts that the business is not large enough to necessitate bringing on an investor partner.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder pivots to discuss intellectual property, noting they have a pending utility patent for the sealed cavity.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks if there are currently many other banana preservation devices on the market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confidently states that they will be the first of their kind.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter jokes about whether there is an official banana preservation society they should be aware of.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder plays along, suggesting they could join the society together if it exists.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter laughs at the founder's quick comeback regarding the fictional society.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond states the business is not large enough to require an investor partner and officially drops out of the deal.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter checks to see if the founder still maintains his full-time job at the investment bank.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms that he does indeed still have his full-time job.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori asks who is currently managing the day-to-day operations of the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states he is the sole employee handling the entire operation.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori asks if he owns one hundred percent of the company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms he owns it entirely, adding that his wife helps and they recently had a baby.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori reacts warmly to the picture of the founder's newborn baby.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter praises the product, saying he likes it and believes it could become highly successful in the market.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter offers to provide half the requested money and tells the founder he will need to find another shark.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori offers to provide the other half of the money, noting their combined international and domestic market reach.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark jokes about the product going global.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter clearly states his terms, asking for fifteen percent equity in exchange for his half of the investment.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori confirms she also wants fifteen percent equity for her share of the investment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder takes a moment to process the joint offer, realizing he has multiple sharks interested.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori highlights the advantage of having two sharks, providing both national and international exposure.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin points out that giving up thirty percent equity is a very aggressive deal structure.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin offers the full requested amount for the asked equity but adds a one dollar per unit royalty.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder laughs and acknowledges Kevin's offer, noting that it is not a terrible alternative.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter points out the math, comparing the ten percent plus royalty to the thirty percent equity deal.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin proposes that Peter ditch Lori and partner with him instead.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori defends Peter, stating he is a man of honor and would not betray their partnership.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that Lori simply slipped on a banana peel to justify cutting her out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder smiles at the playful banter between the sharks.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter jokes about his royal title, claiming a Commander of the British Empire would never behave dishonorably.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin quickly retorts that Peter would absolutely do it if it meant a better deal.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter urges the founder to take the joint deal with him and Lori, calling it a dream ticket.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin warns the founder that he is giving up far too much equity to Peter and Lori.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark suggests the founder ask Kevin how he plans to actively help the business grow.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder asks Peter and Lori if they would be willing to accept fifteen percent equity for the full amount.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter clarifies if the founder means fifteen percent total, meaning they would split it.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori asks Peter if he would be willing to meet the founder at twenty percent total.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder quickly agrees that he would accept a deal at twenty percent equity.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter repeats the twenty percent figure to confirm the terms being discussed.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms the counteroffer of one hundred fifty thousand for twenty percent equity.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori counters the founder's proposal, stating that they will do the deal for twenty percent equity combined.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter gives a thumbs up, indicating his agreement to join Lori's revised offer of twenty percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder agrees to the revised terms of twenty percent equity with Peter and Lori, sealing the deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori cheers as the deal is officially accepted by the founder.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin remarks playfully about the outcome, acknowledging the successful deal closure.

Wants to share the deal with another shark.
Likes the product and wants to partner with Peter.
Wants a royalty structure instead of taking more equity.
Wants to reduce the equity given up to Peter and Lori.
Refuses 15% but lowers the combined equity requirement to 20%.
Gives a thumbs up to Lori's revised 20% total equity.

record.notes: S3 Peter Jones is a guest shark from the UK. The S1-S5 mapping follows their order of first speaking during the Q&A.
